attribution.text: Original Fate's Hand content: all rights reserved. This layer adds `data.blurb` and `data.fiche_stats` fields to the species and class records defined in the System Reference Document 5.2.1 (“SRD 5.2.1”) by Wizards of the Coast LLC, available at https://www.dndbeyond.com/srd, licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, available at https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode, and to the Araag, Elestu and Loroka species original to Fate's Hand. No SRD text is reproduced anywhere in this layer: every blurb is original prose, at most informed by SRD and fh-lore-en concepts summarized in the author's own words, and every fiche_stats value is a compressed derivation of SRD 5.2.1 mechanical data and Fate's Hand skill-pool data (fh-skills-en).

description: Compressed character-sheet text for the twelve playable species and twelve classes of Fate's Hand: a ~50-word blurb (data.blurb) and a compact stat block (data.fiche_stats) sized for the 360px character builder screen. Two records (wizard, fighter) reproduce Eric's own hand-written reference text verbatim (provenance: "eric"); the other twenty-two are original Fate's Hand prose (provenance: "fh-original"). Species records also carry data[fiche_traits]: the short `name — effect` trait lines drawn in the fixed lower half of a species card (lot 78, Eric's croquis A). Species records that offer a lineage carry it in data[fiche_infos] (lot 78b, Eric croquis): it is drawn in its own full-width zone under the top block, not in the stat column. Five species out of twelve offer one (dragonborn 10, goliath 6, elf 3, tiefling 3, gnome 2); the other seven carry no lineage in SRD 5.2.1 nor in fh-species-en, so their band is ABSENT — an empty band would be a false shopfront, and it is that absence which centres their lower half. All twelve classes carry data[fiche_infos] too: SRD 5.2.1 ships exactly one subclass per class (data.subclass), gained at level 3, so the band reads `Subclass : 1 type, at level 3` — an information panel, not a decision organ: no subclass is chosen at level 1.

srd:species:en:dragonborn.note: SRD 5.2.1 species data: creature_type Humanoid, size Medium, speed 30ft, Draconic Ancestry trait (10 named dragon colors) -> Lineages compressed to a count ('10 types') rather than listing all 10, for width. fh-species-en patch only touches destiny, not size/speed/type.

data.blurb.text: A dragonborn's ancestor is an idea more than a specific dragon—an inherited breath weapon, hide to match it, and a posture that never apologizes for the room it takes. Scale color spans the old dragon families, jet to gold, and matters less than a stranger's own bearing. Test either trait, and the temper shows up fast.

srd:species:en:dwarf.note: SRD 5.2.1: Humanoid, Medium, 30ft. No lineage-choice trait -> Lineages omitted.

data.blurb.text: Dwarves don't rush—they've outlasted enough hurried kingdoms; history is measured in mined seams, not crowned heads. Poison barely slows one down, and tunnel-bred eyes see deep into the dark. A dwarf never loses track of who owes what; settle a debt cleanly and the friendship lasts.

srd:species:en:elf.note: SRD 5.2.1 + fh-species-en patch (destiny/description only, not size/speed/type): Humanoid, Medium, 30ft. Elven Lineage trait (3 named options: Drow/High Elf/Wood Elf) -> Lineages compressed to '3 types' for width/consistency. · 27/08 : fiche_lineage_lvl1 = le FORMAT RACCOURCI des niveaux 1 pour les fiches (esprit SRFH — ni SRD ni règle FH, un ajustement de confort ; Eric : « c'est un format raccourci pour entrer dans les fiches »). ⏳ Migrera dans une vraie famille srfh de fh-srd le jour où l'importeur la porte.

data.blurb.text: An elf's lifespan makes 'old' beside the point—centuries wear one down the way a river wears a stone, without breaking it. Sleep is optional; a few hours of trance covers it, and charm slides off an elf's mind. Whatever lineage magic runs in the blood only deepens with age.

data[fiche_lineage_lvl1].drow: Darkvision 120 ft — Dancing Lights cantrip known.
data[fiche_lineage_lvl1].high-elf: Prestidigitation cantrip known — after a Long Rest, replace it with any Wizard cantrip.

srd:species:en:gnome.note: SRD key is srd:species:en:gnome; FH renames the species 'Hoddon' (fh-species-en patch changes data.name/slug). Stats: Humanoid, Small, 30ft, Hoddon Lineage (2 named options: Forest/Rock) -> Lineages compressed to '2 types' for width/consistency with other lineage rows.

data.blurb.text: Meeting a Hoddon is rare, by design—the little folk keep their holds hidden and their business private. Charm, threats, and clever lies mostly bounce off a Hoddon's mind mid-sentence. Some lean toward the deep woods and what lives there, others toward small ingenious contraptions. Either way, trust is earned slowly.

data[fiche_traits].name: Hoddon Cunning
data[fiche_traits].effect: ADV on INT, WIS, CHA SV

srd:species:en:goliath.note: SRD 5.2.1: Humanoid, Medium, speed 35ft (NB: differs from the 30ft default of every other species here). Giant Ancestry trait (6 named giant types) -> Lineages compressed to '6 types'.

data.blurb.text: A goliath's home is wherever the giants haven't burned down yet—hence the build, tall enough to meet most threats eye to eye, and the habit of never settling. Giant blood surfaces when a fight turns ugly, lending power few humanoids can match. Underneath sits an oddly modest wish: a roof that won't need rebuilding next season.

srd:species:en:halfling.note: SRD 5.2.1: Humanoid, Small, 30ft. No lineage-choice trait -> Lineages omitted.

data.blurb.text: Halflings prove patience beats size—the same valley farmed quietly long after the empire next door has fallen twice. Knocked down, a halfling gets up without drama, catching fewer bad breaks than seems fair. Small enough to vanish behind cover that wouldn't hide anyone else, a halfling is easy to underestimate exactly once.

srd:species:en:human.note: SRD 5.2.1: Humanoid, size is a level-1 player choice between Medium and Small -> written «Medium/Small»: the full «Medium or Small» measures 129.9 px for the 118 px stats column at the 360 floor (measured, garde 2), the slash renders 115.1 px and keeps both words whole. No lineage-choice trait -> Lineages omitted.

data.blurb.text: Humans got wiped off the map once and simply refused to stay gone. Outnumbered by older peoples, they compensate in volume: cities built in a hurry, arguments louder than needed, ambitions past what the numbers justify. Having survived erasure, a human treats setbacks as background noise.

srd:species:en:orc.note: SRD 5.2.1: Humanoid, Medium, 30ft. No lineage-choice trait -> Lineages omitted.

data.blurb.text: What outsiders call ferocity is usually just stamina nobody else can match—orcs hold the hard country because they refuse to quit first. The body backs it: a burst of speed under pressure, a refusal to drop the first time death looks likely. An orc sizes people up fast; the only real question is what they can carry, and how far.

Fiendish Legacy trait (3 named legacies: Abyssal/Chthonic/Infernal) -> Lineages compressed to '3 types'.

data.blurb.text: A tiefling's mark reads as trouble before they've done anything to earn it, which teaches most tieflings to charm early, since trust arrives slowly either way. Underneath the easy manner sits something genuinely uncanny: a bloodline granting its own resistance, eyes at home in full dark, and a small trick of magic worth one gesture.

fh:species:en:araag.note: fh-species-en (wholly FH-original record, not an SRD patch): creature_type Humanoid, size Medium, speed 30ft. No lineage-choice trait -> Lineages row omitted. Blurb consistent with fh-lore-en araag lore (Harvest, cost-free soulgem bond, necrotic resistance, darkvision, fast learner).

data.blurb.text: Araags wear the Harvest that ended the last free humans as a mark, not a memory—a soulgem binds into their flesh at no cost, necrotic wounds barely register, and their eyes still read the dark their ancestors fled. Common in the Empire sharing their name, eyed with suspicion beyond it, an Araag learns fast from survival, not ambition.

fh:species:en:elestu.note: fh-species-en (wholly FH-original record): Humanoid, Medium, 30ft. No lineage-choice trait -> Lineages omitted. Blurb consistent with fh-lore-en elestu lore (never-elf, elf+human/Araag parentage, university/Moonkeeper circles, fast learner, charm resistance, trance).

data.blurb.text: An elf paired with a human, or with an Araag, never produces another elf—a fact Elestu spend energy correcting. Too mortal for elves, too strange for everyone else, they cluster around lecture halls and moonlit circles instead: fast learners, charm-resistant, needing no real sleep. Two worlds beats belonging fully to either.

fh:species:en:loroka.note: fh-species-en (wholly FH-original record): Humanoid, Medium, 30ft. No lineage-choice trait -> Lineages omitted. Blurb consistent with fh-lore-en loroka lore (Theymoron highlands, largest population in the capital, Relentless Endurance, soldiering when asked).

data.blurb.text: Loroka worked these terraced hills long before the country had a name, and stayed—today they outnumber every other people in its capital. Knocked to the edge of death, a Loroka's body finds one more breath out of pure stubbornness. Called to the Front, a Loroka picks up a spear, then goes home and picks the hoe back up.

data.blurb.text: Rage isn't losing control—it's the only control a barbarian trusts. Pain fades, caution burns away, and the body remembers a violence older than any drilled stance. They shrug off blows that would drop an armored knight, then hit back twice as hard. No spellbook, no oath: only fury, sharpened by every fight survived.

data.blurb.text: A bard bets a song can do what a sword can't, and wins more than skeptics expect. Charisma isn't decoration here—it's the power source, drawn from music, wit, and nerve rather than study or scripture. They can talk down a guard, then fight the next one, barely noticing. Every performance is a small working of magic.

data.blurb.text: A cleric's power isn't borrowed, it's granted—proof something answered the prayer. The bargain cuts both ways: healing in one hand, judgment in the other, and a debt of service that doesn't clock out after battle. Robes under armor, a holy symbol worth more than the sword. Private life is the calling's first casualty.

data.blurb.text: A druid doesn't dominate nature, they petition it—and get answers more often than a king would like. Ask properly, and weather, root, even a wolf's own body can be borrowed a while; the oldest barely bother turning back. Kingdoms trust borders. A druid was loyal to the ground before any line got drawn.

data.blurb.text: Steel remembers what flesh forgets. Ten thousand strikes forge it. No spellbook, no arcane grammar—only muscle and discipline. They are the wall that never breaks. Armor is their skin; courage is the spell. Knight, duelist, veteran—all built by practice, not birth. When magic fails, steel remains.

data.blurb.text: A monk spent years turning an empty hand into a weapon nobody had to hand them, and their own body into armor nobody had to forge. Somewhere in there they learn to catch a blow mid-flight and send it back. No steel, no plate: just discipline, repeated past where most people quit and call it enough.

data.blurb.text: A paladin's magic comes with strings attached—one oath, sworn once, that the power keeps checking against. Keep it, and the strength holds; bend it for convenience, and the paladin feels it first. They walk into fights cautious people avoid, healing hands as practiced as the blade. The oath is the whole engine.

data.blurb.text: A ranger notices what the ground is trying to hide—a bent stalk, a wrong print, weather an hour before anyone else smells it. Half warrior, half quiet spellcaster, most dangerous at home, oddly at ease around animals that would bolt from anyone else. Rangers walk point, and everyone follows the boot prints.

data.blurb.text: A rogue doesn't overpower a fight, they end it early—one clean opening turns an ordinary hit into the only hit that mattered. That same eye for the gap shows up in a lock, a lie, a guard's blind spot. Jack of a dozen trades and better at leaving unseen, a rogue survives on a second way out already scouted.

data.blurb.text: A sorcerer's magic showed up before any teacher could claim credit—inherited, inborn, or triggered by something that only happened once. It answers to instinct more than study: faster to reach for than a wizard's spell, harder to leash even after years of aiming it. Ask how it works and watch them shrug: it just does.

data.blurb.text: Somewhere past the ordinary rules of magic sits a warlock's patron; what that deal cost is nobody else's business. Invocations are doors that shouldn't exist, forced open once and left unlocked—no study, just payment made. The fine print stays private. What shows is the confidence of someone who no longer asks.

data.blurb.text: Weavers of arcane grammar, wizards bend reality through study, not birth. Spellbooks hold their power—lost pages mean lost magic. They shape fire, bend time, pierce minds, through relentless intellect. Fragile in armor, mighty in will, they trade strength for the universe's deepest secrets, one spell slot at a time.
